builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: AIPC: Evidence-Guided Agent Workflows for PyTorch Project Deployment
summary: AIPC replaces manual, expert-driven PyTorch-to-NPU porting (format conversion, quantization, toolchain configuration, on-target debugging) with an LLM agent guided by structured Skills and toolchain/runtime/profiling evidence. It costs the engineering effort of encoding domain Skills, tool permissions, and check conditions up front, plus LLM inference per run, and the results are tied to the Qualcomm QAIRT toolchain and NPU targets. It can fail when operator support or quantization behavior falls outside the encoded Skills, causing misdiagnosis or drift in large configuration and repair spaces, and the zero-intervention runs depend on a pre-fixed deployment contract that may not hold for novel projects.
rationale: The method targets NPU deployment on a specific vendor toolchain rather than the reader's single-GPU or API-based production setting, so it is relevant to track but not adoptable without that hardware and the QAIRT environment.
technique: Skill-guided LLM agent for PyTorch-to-NPU deployment

claims.statement: AIPC replaces manual, expert-driven PyTorch-to-NPU porting (format conversion, quantization, toolchain configuration, on-target debugging) with an LLM agent guided by structured Skills and toolchain/runtime/profiling evidence. It costs the engineering effort of encoding domain Skills, tool permissions, and check conditions up front, plus LLM inference per run, and the results are tied to the Qualcomm QAIRT toolchain and NPU targets. It can fail when operator support or quantization behavior falls outside the encoded Skills, causing misdiagnosis or drift in large configuration and repair spaces, and the zero-intervention runs depend on a pre-fixed deployment contract that may not hold for novel projects.
YOLO-Worldv2 achieves a 2.791x end-to-end speedup versus 1.599x for the control agent; 6/7 Skill-armed Whisper-Small runs meet accuracy and latency criteria versus 0/6 control runs.
